validated_contracts: The v2 Python runtime inventory classifies every runtime module without overlap or omission.
All 16 stable Python symbols resolve from the installed public facade.
Core API schemas and normative v1 fixtures validate.
The Rust FFI crate passes its lifecycle, status, EVPI, ENBS, and error-transport tests.
The Python wheel black-box tests and current binding workflow declaration tests pass.
The C ABI is deliberately narrow at ten symbols and currently exposes EVPI and ENBS numerical capabilities.
The v2.1.0 released ABI baseline comparison retains every released symbol, declaration, layout, calling convention, and ownership contract; voiage_v1_enbs_r is additive.
The self-contained R source package compiles its package-owned Rust bridge and invokes registered native EVPI and ENBS routines without an ambient shared library.
Julia 1.12 package-quality, EVPI, ENBS, and shared numerical-reference tests pass against the explicit development ABI override; package-managed JLL availability remains an external gate.

findings.summary: The industry binding manifest claims implemented DecisionProblem symbols in Rust, R, and Julia that do not match the shipped surfaces; R and Julia export no such symbol, the Rust type is voiage_domain::DecisionProblem rather than voiage_core::schema::DecisionProblem, and no DecisionProblem C ABI exists.
findings.required_disposition: Correct the manifest to contract-only or implement and test the named surfaces; make validation resolve real symbols and interchange paths instead of asserting manifest text.
findings.resolution: The disposition manifest now identifies the real Python and internal Rust symbols, marks C ABI, R, and Julia DecisionProblem surfaces unsupported, and resolves implemented symbols in a fresh interpreter.

findings.summary: voiageR declares NeedsCompilation: no while requiring an externally supplied voiage-ffi shared library, so its native EVPI and ENBS path is not a self-contained installed R package.
findings.required_disposition: Build and install the Rust bridge as part of the R source package, reconcile NeedsCompilation and SystemRequirements, and prove clean-library installation and execution.
findings.resolution: voiageR declares compilation, builds an allocation-free Rust static library inside the source package, registers package-owned C adapters, and passes clean-library native fixture tests.

findings.summary: The Julia package opens libvoiage_ffi by ambient loader name or VOIAGE_FFI_LIBRARY and has no artifact declaration, build step, or package-managed binary dependency.
findings.required_disposition: Package the native library through a Julia artifact/JLL route or explicitly classify the source package as requiring a separately installed ABI library and test the clean-depot contract.
findings.resolution: The source package and clean-copy development matrix pass on Julia 1.10 through 1.12 and all supported operating systems using the explicit VOIAGE_FFI_LIBRARY development override. JuliaPackaging/Yggdrasil PR #14292 remains open, so package-managed JLL installation is accurately retained as an external gate.

findings.summary: Current symbol and layout snapshots are documentation-tested, but CI does not compare the C ABI against the last released binary/header with an ABI compatibility tool.
findings.required_disposition: Add a release-baseline ABI diff for exported symbols, signatures, layouts, calling convention, and ownership/error behavior; retain the existing runtime tests.
findings.resolution: scripts/check_abi_compatibility.py compares the current header, symbols, and layouts with the immutable v2.1.0 release baseline locally, in bindings CI, and before release; the current diff is compatible.

findings.summary: Python exposes 16 stable symbols while the native R and Julia bindings each expose only EVPI and ENBS; the supported-binding matrix does not provide a method-level capability table for this intentional asymmetry.
findings.required_disposition: Publish and test a method-level binding matrix that distinguishes native, Python-adapter, contract-only, experimental, unsupported, and external-gated capabilities.
findings.resolution: The versioned current-capability matrix and public binding documentation enumerate every stable and experimental method across Python, Rust, C ABI, R, and Julia with explicit asymmetries.

findings.summary: The repository tracks a stale voiageR_0.1.0.tar.gz beside 2.1.0 source metadata, creating an ambiguous installed-artifact candidate.
findings.required_disposition: Remove the stale generated archive from source control after confirming it is not required evidence, and generate source packages only in isolated build output.
findings.resolution: The stale 0.1.0 archive is no longer tracked, and R build/check runners create and address one exact versioned 2.1.0 archive in an isolated temporary directory.

findings.summary: Several binding tests validate that manifests contain expected strings and workflow commands but do not resolve declared symbols from built, installed R and Julia packages.
findings.required_disposition: Add clean-install black-box consumers that enumerate exported symbols, call supported methods, reject unsupported capabilities, and compare serialized numerical fixtures.
findings.resolution: Installed Python, R, C ABI, and Julia checks resolve actual exports, invoke EVPI and ENBS, compare the shared fixture corpus, and keep unsupported capability states explicit.

boundary: Passing current contract and workflow-declaration tests demonstrates internal consistency, not installed cross-language parity or backward ABI compatibility.
